post.caption: Shakespeare's will left money to buy rings. The will is dated 25 March 1616 and has three pages, and three of his six known signatures are on its pages. Three fellow actors each got 26 shillings and 8 pence for rings, and two more friends were left the same sum for a ring each. The actors' ring money was squeezed in between the lines, and one friend named for a ring was crossed out and replaced. Leaving money for memorial rings was a common custom for centuries. A gold ring marked WS found in 1810 is still debated. The original will is kept at The National Archives in Kew.
